answer: Clock-skew fingerprinting: every machine's quartz crystal drifts at its own rate, a few parts per million fast or slow. Each epoch, from dawn to dusk on the ledger clock, every ID signs timestamps on 60 beacon pings; a fit strips out network jitter and leaves that drift as a hardware anchor. IDs whose skew agrees within about 1 ppm across several epochs are read as one box and share one reward, like yarrow stalks found to run from a single root. Faking a distinct, steady drift per clone is fiddly, and one slip links them. Thresholds are my estimates.
